title: Hydra — workflows/<name>.yaml and workflows/thread.yaml
description: A workflow file (several Hydra jobs and actions, expressed as a dependency graph) or the project thread file workflows/thread.yaml (the order in which hdrctl runs the workflows). A file with a top-level 'thread' key is read as the thread file.

version.description: Workflow file DSL version, written by hdrctl init at the top of the file.

threadFile.description: workflows/thread.yaml — execution order of the project's workflows, read by hdrctl run. Stages run one after the other; optional loops replay a part of the thread.

thread.description: Stages, run one after the other.

loops.description: Optional loops: when workflow 'from' finishes, go back to workflow 'to' (earlier in the thread, or the same one) and replay that part. Loops must not overlap.

mode.description: sequential: the stage's workflows run one after the other. parallel: they run at the same time.

delay_after.description: Pause after the stage: a number of seconds, or a duration such as 30s, 5m, 1h, 500ms.

active.description: false: hdrctl run skips this workflow without removing it (debugging).

delay_before.description: Wait before starting this workflow: a number of seconds, or 500ms, 30s, 5m, 1h. Sequential stage: counted from the end of the previous workflow. Parallel stage: from the start of the stage (staggered starts). Fallback conditions are checked after the wait; in a parallel stage, a failure cancels the starts still waiting.

timeout.description: Maximum duration of one run of this workflow (and of each fallback run in its place): a number of seconds, or 30s, 5m, 1h (more than 0). Beyond it the workflow is stopped at the next step or batch (an all-or-nothing load is cancelled; an action already started finishes) and counts as failed; with fallback.on_failure, the fallback can then run.

threadFallback.description: Backup workflow(s) for this workflow. The fallbacks are workflows/<name>.yaml files that are NOT in the thread; one takes this workflow's place when 'when' is true just before the start, or after a failure if 'on_failure' is true.

use.description: Fallback workflow(s), tried in order. A name or a list of names.

when.description: Condition checked just before the start. Functions: source_available('name'), destination_available('name'), file_exists('path'), file_size('path'), file_age('path'), url_ok('url'), secret_defined('name'), db.load('name'); values: previous.status, previous.rows; operators: and, or, not, ==, !=, <, <=, >, >=; durations 30s, 5m, 24h, 7d; sizes 10KB, 5MB, 1GB.

on_failure.description: true: also switch to the fallback after this workflow fails or exceeds its timeout, only if it left nothing published (no load published and no outside action done, or everything undone by rollback: true). If the fallback fails too, the next one in 'use' runs. Otherwise the project stops and says why.

on_probe_error.description: If a check of 'when' fails or times out: keep the planned workflow (default) or switch to the fallback.

from.description: Workflow at the end of the loop: when it finishes, the run goes back to 'to'.

to.description: Workflow where the loop starts again. Must come before 'from' in the thread (or be the same workflow).

times.description: Number of passes in total (2 = this part of the thread runs twice).

delay.description: Pause before each repeat: a number of seconds, or a duration such as 30s, 5m, 1h, 500ms.

name.description: Workflow name. Appears in logs and run results.

rollback.description: If the workflow fails, undo the steps already done, the last one first: jobs are undone automatically (previous file or table content, added rows removed); actions that act outside Hydra (webhook, email, bash, powershell, ssh, python) need 'undo'. Checked before the run: a database append needs load.key. An unfinished undo is completed with 'hdrctl workflow undo <name>'.

steps.description: Workflow steps. Execution order is driven by 'depends_on', not by list order. Step names must be unique.

enumDescriptions: manual — started on demand with hdrctl workflow run.
schedule — started automatically according to 'cron'. The 'cron' field becomes required.
webhook — started by an incoming HTTP call.

cron.description: Five-field cron expression: minute hour day month weekday. Required when type is 'schedule'.

name.description: Step identifier, unique within the workflow. Other steps refer to it in their 'depends_on'.

enumDescriptions: job — runs a Hydra job. The 'job' field becomes required.
action — runs a built-in action. The 'action' field becomes required.

job.description: Path to the job directory, relative to workflow.yaml. The directory must contain sources.yaml, destinations.yaml and pipeline.yaml.

enumDescriptions: log — write a message to the workflow log.
delay — pause the workflow.
condition — evaluate an expression and branch on the result.
webhook — send an HTTP request.
email — send an email.
bash — run a shell command (Linux/macOS).
powershell — run a PowerShell command (Windows).
ssh — run a command on a remote host.
python — run Python code.
set_param — define a runtime parameter for later steps.
assign_param — assign a computed value to a runtime parameter.

params.description: Action parameters. Values may reference a runtime parameter using the {{ param:NAME }} syntax.

depends_on.description: Names of the steps that must finish before this one. An empty list starts the step immediately. Steps sharing the same dependencies run in parallel.

on_failure.description: What happens when this step fails.
enumDescriptions: fail — stop the workflow. The default; keep it for critical steps.
skip — mark the step as skipped and carry on.
continue — carry on despite the failure.

enabled.description: Set to false to disable a step without deleting it from the file.

when.description: Conditional guard: the step runs only when the expression is true.

undo.description: type=action only. How to reverse this action when the workflow (rollback: true) fails after it: an action, or 'none' (nothing to reverse).

action.description: Action that reverses the step (same actions and params as a step).

retryPolicy.description: Retry policy applied when the step fails.

max.description: Number of retries AFTER the first failure. 0 disables retrying.

backoff.description: How the delay evolves between attempts.
enumDescriptions: fixed — constant delay.
exponential — delay doubles on each attempt. Recommended for network calls.
